nws_afd.text:
000
FXUS66 KMTR 211551
AFDMTR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Francisco CA
751 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

...New UPDATE...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 1259 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

 - Cold temperatures this morning

 - Light to moderate rain showers Saturday and Sunday

 - Moderate coastal flooding Saturday followed by major to extreme 
   coastal flooding Thanksgiving week

 - Impactful storm next Tuesday and Wednesday

 - Storm door remains open beyond the current extended forecast

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 749 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

Satellite imagery reveals high clouds streaming into the region
while patches of fog and stratus persist inland and near the
higher elevations. Expect the stratus to be slow to mix out with
the high clouds filtering incoming solar radiation and limiting
heating. The Cold Weather Advisory has been allowed to expire with
temperatures beginning to warm above Advisory criteria. 

DialH

&&

.SHORT TERM...
Issued at 1259 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026
(Today and tonight)

Weak upper level ridging will be replaced by the next upper trough 
swinging through the west coast. Ahead of it clear skies will lead 
to a chilly start for Saturday morning. A Cold Weather Advisory is 
in effect through 8 AM Saturday morning for the inland North Bay, 
interior East Bay, eastern Santa Clara Hills, the Santa Lucia 
mountains, the southern Salinas Valley, and the interior Central 
Coast mountains seeing low temperatures in the lower to middle 30s. 
Elsewhere, chilly temperatures are forecast as well, ranging from 
the upper 30s to low 40s and the mid to upper 40s along the 
immediate coastline. High temperatures will rebound into the 50s for 
most interior valley locations, with areas of higher terrain only 
creeping into the upper 30s to near 50 degrees. The next weather 
system will bring an increase in clouds helping suppress 
temperature growth in addition to rain showers. Precipitation 
slowly spreads south towards the North Bay by mid to late day, and
making to to the Central Coast late Saturday afternoon or 
evening. Temperatures Saturday night into Sunday should be similar
Friday night into Saturday, perhaps a few degrees warmer. Post 
frontal showers linger into Sunday.

&&

.LONG TERM...
Issued at 1259 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026
(Sunday through Friday)

Monday we'll see a brief reprieve from the rain, but this will be 
short lived as the next storm system barrels towards the west coast. 
This should be the best day, ahead of Saturday's rain, to work on
preparations for the upcoming storm. To help prepare your 
properties for the next storm, consider clearing storm drains, 
cleaning gutters, and making sure emergency kits are stocked.

Come Tuesday the next storm system arrives bringing with it 
significant rainfall and wind concerns. This system looks to tap 
into some tropical moisture, leading to moderate to heavy rain from 
Tuesday into Wednesday, with shower lingering behind it. A strong 
pressure gradient will set up with this system, bringing wind gusts 
of 25-35 mph for interior valley locations and 40-50 mph winds along 
the coast, through favored gaps and passes, and within the Salinas 
Valley. Add this hazard on top of the upcoming Kind Tides and storm 
surge, and you've got a recipe for difficult travel periods during 
Thanksgiving week. 

We may get a brief break in the weather on Thanksgiving; however, 
the coastal flood threat will hold into the weekend. The storm door 
also remains open into the end November. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 338 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

Currently MVFR-VFR with patchy fog/stratus and high clouds streaming 
in from the west. Light/drainage winds this morning will veer to 
become southerly this afternoon ahead of a cold front, further 
veering to become northwesterly behind it. The best chances for rain 
will be this evening, spreading from northwest to southeast between 
02Z and 12Z. Intermittent MVFR conditions will be possible in the 
form of MVFR ceilings and visibilities. MVFR ceilings may try to 
develop in the post-frontal environment; however, the forecast is 
hedging on drier air funneling in.

Vicinity of SFO...Currently VFR with southwesterly flow. 
Southeasterly winds are expected through the morning, backing and 
increasing to become southerly this afternoon ahead of the cold 
front and northwesterly behind it by this evening. Clouds will 
lower through the afternoon/evening with the best chance for rain 
between 05Z and 09Z. Intermittent MVFR conditions are possible 
with rain in the form of MVFR ceilings and visibilities.

SFO Bridge Approach...Clouds at or below FL070 will begin to filter 
in this afternoon from the northwest, likely impacting the San Mateo 
Bridge Approach by 01Z.

Monterey Bay Terminals...Currently VFR with drainage flow at both 
terminals. Winds will diminish and veer to become southerly this 
afternoon with drainage winds returning this evening. Clouds will 
lower through the TAF period with the best chances for rain beyond 
the 24 hour forecast.

&&

.MARINE...
(Today through Thursday)
Issued at 338 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

A cold front will bring rain this afternoon into this evening
with southerly breezes ahead of it and northwesterly breezes
behind it. Another round of rainfall is expected Sunday morning
into the afternoon with the most impactful likely Tuesday into
Wednesday. Moderate to rough seas will prevail through Monday
with hazardous conditions across the northern outer waters Sunday
and Monday for 10 foot seas. Strong to near gale southerly breezes
will spread from north to south across the waters Monday into
Tuesday. Seas will build to become rough to very rough as a
result.

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 401 PM PST Fri Nov 20 2026

A Coastal Flood Advisory in effect for the San Francisco Bay 
until 6 AM PST Monday, at which point it will be upgraded to a 
Coastal Flood Warning through Thursday. A Coastal Flood Advisory 
is in effect for the Pacific Coast from Saturday through Thursday.
At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.5
ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM Saturday, 2.1 ft above 
normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.3 ft above normal (8.1 
ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 
10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM 
Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM 
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that 
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide 
varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast 
and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

&&

.MTR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
CA...Coastal Flood Advisory until 6 AM PST Monday for CAZ006-506-508.

     Coastal Flood Warning from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday for 
     CAZ006-506-508.

     Coastal Flood Advisory until 4 PM PST Thursday for CAZ505-509-
     529-530.

PZ...Small Craft Advisory from 9 PM this evening to 9 AM PST Monday 
     for Pt Arena to Pt Reyes 10-60 NM.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...KR
LONG TERM....KR
AVIATION...Sarment
MARINE...Sarment

Visit us at www.weather.gov/sanfrancisco

nws_alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 20 at 2:52PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
nws_alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.1 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 3.0 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday, 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday,
2.3 ft above normal (8.1 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft
above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above
normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above
normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions
include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical
tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes
earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San
Francisco Bay, respectively.
